learningObjective: Define TPOT (Time Per Output Token) and distinguish it from TTFT and throughput.

canonicalClaims.claim: TPOT is the average time between successive output tokens (after the first) per request; total request latency = TTFT + (M-1)*TPOT for M output tokens.
conditions: Metric is per-request; server aggregates report percentiles.
Assumes streaming so per-token times are measurable.
nonImplications: Does not equal throughput per concurrent user.

misconceptions.whyWrong: That is a per-user throughput calculation, not TPOT.
TPOT is defined over decode intervals after the first token.

misconceptions.claim: TPOT is constant across generation steps.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Growing KV cache and batching dynamics can make later tokens slower.

implementationFacts: TPOT is directly proportional to KV cache read bandwidth per token at batch-1 decode.
Speculative decoding attempts to lower effective TPOT by producing multiple tokens per verification step.
performanceScenarios: SLA-driven serving often has a TPOT target (e.g., <50 ms/token) that must be preserved even under load.
